# RedwoodSDK: Type-Safe Navigation with linkFor

## Background
A RedwoodSDK project is pre-installed at `/home/user/myapp`. Use `linkFor` from `rwsdk/router` to build a typed `link` helper, and use it inside server components so that every link in your HTML output is generated from the typed helper (no hard-coded path strings on the page).

## Requirements
Extend `src/worker.tsx` with the routes below (all under the existing `render(Document, ...)` block) and create a `src/app/shared/links.ts` file that exports a typed `link` constant created from `linkFor<App>()` (where `App` is the type of the default export from `src/worker.tsx`). Use that `link` helper inside the page components.

- `GET /home`: server component HTML must contain an `<a>` element whose `href` is generated by calling `link("/about")` and whose visible text is `About`. It must also contain an `<a>` whose `href` is generated by calling `link("/users/:id", { id: "42" })` and whose visible text is `Show user 42`.
- `GET /about`: HTML must contain an `<a>` whose `href` is generated by calling `link("/home")` and whose visible text is `Back to home`.
- `GET /users/:id`: HTML must contain the text `User profile: <id>` (with the URL param substituted).

The `RoutePaths` extracts paths from `RouteDefinition<infer Path, any>`.

Actually it's the reverse: the handler expects `{ params: { id: string } }` but receives `{ params: any }`. Since `any` is assignable to `{ id: string }`, that's fine. I've extended the RedwoodSDK project with type-safe navigation using `linkFor`. Here's a summary of the changes:

## `src/app/shared/links.ts` (already present, verified correct)
Exports a typed `link` constant created from `linkFor<App>()`, where `App` is the type of the default export from `src/worker.tsx` (declared in `types/rw.d.ts`). This gives compile-time type checking of route paths and their params.

## `src/worker.tsx`
Added three new routes under the existing `render(Document, [...])` block (keeping the original `/` route intact):
- `route("/home", HomePage)`
- `route("/about", AboutPage)`
- `route("/users/:id", UserProfile)`

Because these route paths are part of the `defineApp` routes array, the `linkFor<App>()` helper knows about them and type-checks every `link(...)` call.

## New server component pages (no hard-coded path strings)

**`src/app/pages/HomePage.tsx`** — `GET /home`
- An `<a>` whose `href` is `link("/about")` with visible text `About`
- An `<a>` whose `href` is `link("/users/:id", { id: "42" })` with visible text `Show user 42`

**`src/app/pages/AboutPage.tsx`** — `GET /about`
- An `<a>` whose `href` is `link("/home")` with visible text `Back to home`

**`src/app/pages/UserProfile.tsx`** — `GET /users/:id`
- Renders the text `User profile: <id>` with the URL param substituted from `params.id`

All three pages import the typed `link` helper from `@/app/shared/links`, so every `href` is generated from the type-safe helper rather than a hard-coded string. Both `tsc --noEmit` and `vite build` pass cleanly.
